newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Koor Q4 earnings per ADR unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Koor Q4 earnings per ADR unchanged.

text.p: Israel's Koor Industries Ltd
(in thousands of shekels except EPS)
Earnings per share 5.23 5.35 38.82 38.81
Earnings per ADR 1.06 1.06 7.76 7.76

Koor said that in dollar terms, revenues were $3.525 billion last year, with operating income reaching $301.39 million. Net profit was $180.84 million, which worked out to $11.94 per share and $2.39 per American depositary receipt (ADR).
The company did not provide 1995 or quarterly comparative dollar figures.

Koor, Israel's largest holding company, said the 8.4 percent increase in 1996 net earnings included a $21 million capital gain from an initial public offering in Tadiran Telecommunications Ltd, a subsidiary of Koor's 64 percent-owned Tadiran Ltd.

Exports increased 4.4 percent in shekel terms during 1996 to 4.035 billion shekels and 11.1 percent in dollar terms to $1.238 billion. It attributed the difference in growth to the gap between inflation and the shekel-dollar exchange rate.
"Overall, we are satisfied with the results achieved in a difficult business environment," Koor CEO Benjamin Gaon said in a statement.
Koor said the board had declared a dividend of 4.125 shekels per share, or $1.28, which is equal to 0.825 per ADR, or $0.254, payable on May 20 to shareholders of record as of May 6.

Gaon said Koor's strategic businesses -- telecommunications and electronics, agrochemcials, and building and infrastructure materials -- accounted for 77 percent of consolidated revenues and 89 percent of operating income.

"We plan to expand our existing activities in these areas by acquiring new holdings in industrial and marketing enterprises, both in Israel and abroad," he said. "Our goal is for international activities to account for 40 percent of sales in 1997 and 50 percent in the year 2000."
Koor's fourth-quarter revenues were down 1.2 percent from a year earlier. Higher marketing and general and administrative expenses caused operating income to decline 15.8 percent in the quarter.

Gaon noted that Koor's telecommunications group had signed a series of strategic agreements with international companies, including the sale of 20 percent of Telrad to Canada's Nortel and 26 percent of Tadiran Appliances Ltd to Carrier Corp.

"Joining forces with these prestigous concerns will enhance our marketing and development activities, and we have only begun to expore the opportunities they are opening to us," he said in a statement.
Gaon pointed to the building-materials segment as the most problematic for Koor because of Israel's slowing construction sector.

"Nevertheless, we remain focused on anticipated long-term demand and recently completed construction of cement mill no. 10 in Ramle and the cement silo in Haifa," Gaon said, adding that demand was expected to grow from major infrastructure projects now under development in Israel.
He said Koor's agrochemical businesses -- Makhteshim Chemicals and Agan Chemical Manufacturers -- had increased revenues 14.5 percent for the year and exports by 24.4 percent.
"International acquisitions both complement our regional activities and offset the influence of local economic factors on our results," Gaon said.
($1=3.36 shekels)
